title: Geometric Constraints for Small Language Models to Understand and Expand Scientific Taxonomies
claim: Local hierarchy neighbors of a query node can be turned into LLM-augmented edge descriptions that give structured context for placing it.
layout: 2 panels: LLM prompt/response text left, annotated taxonomy tree right with legend
description: The left panel shows a dashed prompt box asking an LLM (o1 logo) to describe the relationship and definitions of target terms, 'protein' and 'peptide elongation factors', with their parent relationships. Below it is the LLM's colour-coded answer. It gives definitions for glycoproteins, proteins and peptide elongation factors, then relationship sentences such as 'Glycoproteins → Proteins'. The right panel shows a vertical taxonomy tree. Colour-coded circles mark the parent node p (red), its ancestors p′ and p″ (fading red), the child node c (blue) with descendants c′ and c″ (fading blue), and the closest (pink) and furthest (purple) siblings. A green star marks the query node q. Small document icons sit beside each node, and coloured webpage icons sit on each edge. A legend at the bottom explains raw node descriptions versus LLM-augmented edge descriptions.
caption: Scientific Taxonomy with LLM Augmentation (Edge-Level).
abstract: Recent findings reveal that token embeddings of Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit strong hyperbolicity. This insight motivates leveraging LLMs for scientific taxonomy tasks, where maintaining and expanding hierarchical knowledge structures is critical. Although potential, generally-trained LLMs face challenges in directly handling domain-specific taxonomies, including computational cost and hallucination. Meanwhile, Small Language Models (SLMs) provide a more economical alternative if empowered with proper knowledge transfer. In this work, we introduce SS-Mono (Structure-Semantic Monotonization), a novel pipeline that combines local taxonomy augmentation from LLMs, self-supervised fine-tuning of SLMs with geometric constraints, and LLM calibration. Our approach enables efficient and accurate taxonomy expansion across root, leaf, and intermediate nodes. Extensive experiments on both leaf and non-leaf expansion benchmarks demonstrate that a fine-tuned SLM (e.g., DistilBERT-base-110M) consistently outperforms frozen LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o, Gemma-2-9B) and domain-specific baselines. These findings highlight the promise of lightweight yet effective models for structured knowledge enrichment in scientific domains.
